title: Activation of BMPR1b-SMAD pathway by Ginsenoside F1 restores osteoblast function in ovariectomy-induced osteoporosis.
authors: Mukherjee, Sulagna; Ko, Il-Gyu; Park, Soo-Young; Seo, Min-Hee; Im, Seung-Soon
one_liner_zh: 该文研究人参皂苷F1通过BMPR1b-SMAD通路促进成骨分化治疗骨质疏松，核心是细胞信号通路与疾病模型，无蛋白质-DNA互作、结合位点预测或AI/物理模拟方法，与本课题无关。
abstract: INTRODUCTION: Osteoblasts are bone-building cells that drive osteogenesis by producing osteoid and promoting its mineralization during development and remodeling. Although ginsenosides from Panax species can enhance bone formation and inhibit resorption, the role of ginsenoside F1 in osteoblast differentiation and bone metabolism has not been defined. OBJECTIVES: This study aimed to elucidate the molecular mechanism by which ginsenoside F1 promotes osteoblast differentiation and evaluate its therapeutic potential in an ovariectomy-induced osteoporosis model. METHODS: Bone marrow-derived mesenchymal stem cells and primary osteoblasts were treated with ginsenoside F1. Osteogenic differentiation was analyzed through gene and protein expression of key markers, including Runx2, Sp7 and Alpl. RNA-sequencing, molecular docking, and siRNA-mediated gene silencing were performed to identify and validate F1's target signaling pathway. The in vivo efficacy of F1 was assessed in ovariectomized mice using micro-computed tomography, histological staining, and biochemical assays. RESULTS: Gene and protein expression analyses showed higher levels of osteogenic transcription factors in F1-induced osteoblasts than in untreated cells. RNA-sequencing analysis and molecular docking studies revealed an association between bone morphogenetic protein receptor type 1b (BMPR1b) and SMAD proteins important for mediating osteoblast differentiation following F1 induction. Furthermore, BMPR1B knockdown attenuated the inhibition of downstream SMAD1/5/9 signaling, indicating that BMP-activated SMAD signaling was required for the pre-osteogenic action of F1. In addition, F1 treatment increased bone mass in ovariectomy-induced osteoporosis. CONCLUSION: Collectively, these findings suggest that ginsenoside F1 enhances osteoblast differentiation and promotes bone formation under osteoporotic conditions, highlighting its therapeutic potential for bone metabolism disorders.
abstract_zh: 引言：成骨细胞是骨形成细胞，通过产生类骨质并在发育和重塑过程中促进其矿化来驱动骨生成。尽管来自人参属的ginsenosides可增强骨形成并抑制骨吸收，但ginsenoside F1在成骨细胞分化和骨代谢中的作用尚未明确。目的：本研究旨在阐明ginsenoside F1促进成骨细胞分化的分子机制，并评估其在卵巢切除诱导的骨质疏松模型中的治疗潜力。方法：用ginsenoside F1处理骨髓来源的间充质干细胞和原代成骨细胞。通过关键标志物（包括Runx2、Sp7和Alpl）的基因和蛋白表达分析成骨分化。采用RNA测序、分子对接和siRNA介导的基因沉默来识别并验证F1的靶向信号通路。在卵巢切除小鼠中，使用显微计算机断层扫描、组织学染色和生化检测评估F1的体内疗效。结果：基因和蛋白表达分析显示，F1诱导的成骨细胞中成骨转录因子水平高于未处理细胞。RNA测序分析和分子对接研究揭示了骨形态发生蛋白受体1b型（BMPR1b）与SMAD蛋白之间的关联，这对F1诱导后介导成骨细胞分化至关重要。此外，BMPR1B敲低减弱了下游SMAD1/5/9信号传导的抑制，表明BMP激活的SMAD信号传导是F1前成骨作用所必需的。另外，F1处理增加了卵巢切除诱导的骨质疏松中的骨量。结论：综合这些发现表明，ginsenoside F1在骨质疏松条件下增强成骨细胞分化并促进骨形成，凸显了其在骨代谢疾病中的治疗潜力。
